setup.title: GitHub connection and event automation
setup.intro: PR reviews and Workflow diagnosis use the selected GitHub system integration. Manage credentials in System integrations; this view never receives secrets.
setup.events.title: Supported events
setup.events.opened: Review a newly opened or reopened PR.
setup.events.ready: Review a draft PR after it is marked ready for review.
setup.events.synchronize: Review new commits on an existing PR, with a 30-second wait to combine consecutive updates. This does not require a separate Push subscription.
setup.events.failure: Diagnose a completed workflow whose conclusion is failure, including runs without a PR.
setup.events.timeout: Diagnose a completed workflow whose conclusion is timed_out, including runs without a PR.
setup.events.filters: Each trigger must be enabled in the repository rules. Draft PRs are skipped; bot-authored PRs are skipped unless included. Branch names match exactly: PR rules use the target branch, Workflow rules use the run branch. Workflow names also match exactly; empty filters include all names or branches.
setup.events.unsupported: Only the conditions above start tasks. Issues, comments, review requests, standalone push events, releases, check_run/check_suite, and PR closing or merging are not supported triggers. Successful, cancelled or skipped workflows do not start diagnosis.
setup.app.title: 1. Configure the GitHub App
setup.app.statusHelp: This status checks the saved App parameters only. It does not verify credentials, installation access, event subscriptions or webhook connectivity. It may appear configured before a Webhook secret is added.
setup.app.permissions: Under Repository permissions, grant Contents: Read and Pull requests: Read & write. Under Subscribe to events, select Pull request. For Workflow failure or timeout diagnosis, also grant Actions: Read and select Workflow run.
setup.app.integration: In Settings → System integrations, configure the same App's App ID, App slug, Client ID, Client Secret, PEM private key and Webhook secret. Select this integration in the Code Review plugin configuration.
setup.app.credentials: Client ID and Client Secret are used for account OAuth authorization; the PEM private key authenticates the App for repository access. Webhook events require a matching secret in GitHub and the system integration. This plugin requires at least 32 characters and rejects deliveries with missing or invalid signatures.
setup.app.install: Enable the App's webhook, configure its Webhook URL and secret, then install the App on the selected repositories. If you later add permissions, approve the updated installation permissions for those repositories.
setup.app.webhookLabel: Webhook URL (based on the current API address)
setup.app.webhookHelp: This is a suggested address, not the URL read back from GitHub. GitHub must be able to reach it over public HTTPS, including during local tests. For local testing, use an HTTPS tunnel to the backend and keep /api/code_review/github/webhook as the path; update GitHub if the tunnel address changes. GitHub cannot reach localhost directly.
setup.app.oauthHelp: Configure the User authorization callback URL separately using the address required by the GitHub connector (path: /api/connector/oauth/callback). It returns users after account authorization; the Webhook URL receives events. These are different URLs.
setup.account.title: 2. Authorize a GitHub account (shared in the workspace)
setup.account.connect: On Repositories, click Connect GitHub and authorize with GitHub App OAuth using the selected system integration. The connection is shared in the workspace. If it uses another integration or a PAT, disconnect it in workspace connector settings before reconnecting; this also affects other users of that shared connection.
setup.account.access: The authorizing account needs write or admin access to the target repository, and the App must be installed with access to it. Account authorization and App installation are separate grants; both are required for repository automation.
setup.rules.title: 3. Choose execution and enable events
setup.rules.repository: Add owner/repository on Repositories, then open Configure rules. Choose the execution mode, event triggers, branch and Workflow filters, and the daily limit.
setup.rules.assistant: Publish a Code Review Assistant and bind the repository to it. Rules reuse the Assistant's existing account. Enable repository rules and the GitHub event subscription. Shared results follow Assistant access; historical private reviews stay private. GitHub publishing remains a separate action.
setup.rules.pipeline: Project pipeline: bind an available Code Review Project pipeline and enable the repository rules. This mode handles PR review events only. Evidence follows Project access, and publication follows the pipeline's human approval gate.
setup.rules.runtime: Events run on the server without Bosi staying open. The backend, queue, webhook, published Assistant account and model must remain available. PR reviews, trials and Workflow diagnosis share the repository daily limit (UTC). Pausing retains history.
setup.verify.title: 4. Verify PR and Workflow events separately
setup.verify.trial: First try an open, non-draft PR number with Try review (no publishing). Confirm the model and result work. A trial does not test webhook delivery or prove that automatic events are enabled.
setup.verify.pr: With the PR rule enabled, open or reopen a non-draft PR, mark a draft ready, or push a commit to an existing PR, according to the selected trigger. Check GitHub's webhook delivery history, then the review inbox and run history. Commit updates wait at least 30 seconds.
setup.verify.workflow: For Workflow diagnosis, select Current Assistant and enable the failure or timeout rule and the Assistant automation. Run a safe test workflow that fails, or use a matching completed failure/timeout delivery. Check GitHub's delivery history, the Assistant task and Workflow diagnosis for the result.
setup.verify.delivery: A valid delivery returns HTTP 202; this alone does not prove a task started or completed. Unmatched events can be ignored or skipped. If no result appears, check repository access, both Assistant-mode switches, event and branch filters, Workflow names, daily quota and execution errors. Duplicate deliveries are deduplicated and do not necessarily create another run.
automation.error.github_integration_unav: The selected GitHub system integration is unavailable in this tenant.
automation.error.github_oauth_unavailabl: The Connector does not provide the required GitHub OAuth integration method. Update the GitHub Connector plugin.
automation.error.github_integration_inco: Complete the App ID, App slug, OAuth and PEM fields in System integrations.
automation.error.github_integration_mism: The shared connection uses another integration or PAT. Disconnect it in workspace connector settings, then return here to authorize with the required integration.
automation.error.github_repository_reval: The GitHub App reference changed. Save the repository rules again to revalidate access.
automation.error.github_app_invalid_key: The GitHub App private key is invalid. Ask an administrator to replace the PEM value.
automation.error.github_app_not_configur: Ask an administrator to configure the GitHub App first.
automation.error.github_auth_required: Connect GitHub with access to this repository.
automation.error.connector_not_installed: Install the GitHub Connector plugin first.
automation.error.repository_management_r: Repository write or admin access is required.
automation.error.installation_permission: Grant the GitHub App Contents read and Pull requests write access.
automation.error.organization_adoption_r: An organization manager must adopt and authorize this legacy policy. Historical access stays unchanged.
automation.error.execution_binding_requi: Bind the execution Assistant and Project before enabling automation.
automation.error.execution_authorization: Execution authority was revoked or is unavailable. Ask an administrator to review and rebind.
automation.error.publication_reconciliat: Resolve active reviews and uncertain publications before rebinding.
automation.error.repository_owned_elsewh: This repository is managed by another organization. Contact a platform administrator.
automation.error.repository_already_conf: This repository already has an automation owner.
automation.error.policy_changed: Policy changed; the next matching PR event will use the new policy.
automation.error.new_commit: A newer commit superseded this review.
automation.error.daily_limit_reached: Daily limit reached (UTC); new events resume tomorrow.
automation.error.review_timeout: Review timed out; check the model and execution.
automation.error.HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED: Review complete; awaiting human approval in the Project pipeline.
automation.error.submission_unknown_chec: Delivery is uncertain. Check GitHub; automatic retries are stopped.
automation.your.account.verifies.reposit: Your account verifies repository authority. The GitHub App receives events and publishes reviews. The bound Assistant runs automation using its own technical account. New evidence follows Assistant or Project access; historical private reviews remain unchanged.
automation.github.connection.status.is.t: GitHub connection status is temporarily unavailable. Refresh to try again.
GitHub App is not configured. An administrator must configure it before enabling automation. You can still try public PRs in the inbox.
automation.repository.name: Repository name
automation.rules.retain.the.bound.assist: Rules retain the bound Assistant. Rebinding is a separate action and leaves automation paused.
automation.the.policy.will.use.this.assi: The policy will use this Assistant’s technical account and stay paused. Historical private reviews remain private.
automation.stops.new.and.subsequent.exec: Stops new and subsequent execution while retaining configuration and history.
automation.base.branches.one.per.line.em: Base branches (one per line; empty means all)
assistantHelp: Automation uses the bound Assistant’s technical account. New results follow Assistant access; historical private results remain private. After saving, enable GitHub events in the execution Assistant’s Automation settings.
automation.binding.preview: Bind Assistant “{{assistant}}” in workspace “{{workspace}}”, reuse its technical account, and leave automation paused. Historical private reviews remain private.
automation.assistant.binding.required: Select and save the executing Assistant
